title: Orientation-Driven Natural Ventilation and Thermal Comfort in a Standardized Egyptian School Prototype: A Validated CFD and Multi-Metric Comfort Assessment
content: Standardized school prototypes are replicated across Egypt regardless of local wind, yet the effect of courtyard orientation on classroom ventilation and summer comfort remains poorly quantified. This study assessed a five-story prototype in hot-arid Cairo using validated non-isothermal computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for four courtyard orientations (0°, 15°, 30° and 45° relative to the prevailing August wind), combined with adaptive and heat-balance comfort indices. The realizable k–ε model reproduced measured classroom temperatures with a root-mean-square error of 0.31 K, and discretization uncertainty was below 1.5%. The wind-aligned layout gave the highest mean classroom air speed (0.44 m/s) and the lowest air temperature (31.1 °C); rotations of 15–45° reduced air speed by 19–29% and raised air temperature by 1.5–4.0 K, well above the model uncertainty. No orientation met the 80% acceptability limit of the ASHRAE 55 adaptive model (30.4 °C). The aligned classroom would comply only with ceiling fans providing at least 0.6 m/s, whereas rotated layouts would also need substantial heat-gain reductions; Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 projections indicate that this margin is exhausted at about 2 K of regional warming. Courtyard alignment is necessary but insufficient and must be combined with elevated air movement and heat-gain control.
